quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “hot”?
quests.hint: Imagine holding an ice cube in your bare hand.
quests.explanation: Hot and cold sit at opposite ends of how things feel to touch. Fresh soup is hot; an ice pop is the other way around.
quests.funFact: The English word “hot” comes from the Old English word “hāt”.

quests.instruction: An elephant stands beside a tiny mouse. The elephant is big, so the mouse is…
quests.hint: Picture which animal you could hold in your cupped hands.
quests.explanation: Big means something takes up lots of space. Small is the other side of that: it needs only a little room.
quests.funFact: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived.

quests.instruction: The kite zoomed up into the sky. When the wind stopped, it floated…
quests.hint: What happens to a ball once you stop throwing it higher?
quests.explanation: Up means toward the sky and down means toward the ground. Without wind pushing it, the kite came back toward the ground.
quests.funFact: Astronauts floating in orbit don’t feel any up or down the way we do on Earth.

quests.instruction: The cat is in the box. Which word is the opposite of “in”?
quests.hint: Picture the cat stepping from the box onto the kitchen floor.
quests.explanation: In means inside something. Out means on the outside of it, like the cat hopping to the floor.
quests.funFact: We use “in” and “out” in many phrases, like “in a hurry” and “out of order”.

quests.instruction: The window was open all afternoon. At night it got chilly, so Mia wanted it…
quests.hint: Think of the last chilly night, just before bed.
quests.explanation: Open means there’s a gap that air and people can pass through. Closed means that gap is covered up.
quests.funFact: Most shop doors have a sign with “open” on one side and “closed” on the other.

quests.instruction: A cheetah is fast. A garden snail is…
quests.hint: Think about how long it would take each animal to cross the playground.
quests.explanation: Fast things cover a lot of ground quickly. Slow things take their time to go the same distance.
quests.funFact: A cheetah is the fastest land animal, but it can only run that fast for short bursts.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “day”?
quests.hint: When do the stars come out above your street?
quests.explanation: Day is the bright part of the 24 hours when the sun is up. Night is the dark part when the sun is on the other side of the Earth.
quests.funFact: Earth spins around once about every 24 hours, which gives us one day and one night.

quests.instruction: Sam’s ice cream fell onto the pavement. He wasn’t happy anymore. He felt…
quests.hint: Your face tells the story: picture how the corners of your mouth droop.
quests.explanation: Happy is a bright, cheerful feeling. Sad is the heavy, droopy feeling that comes when something upsets you.
quests.funFact: Many emoji use an upturned mouth for happy and a downturned mouth for sad.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “clean”? (your hands right after washing vs. after digging in mud)
quests.hint: Look at the soles of your shoes after a walk through a muddy puddle.
quests.explanation: Clean means free from dirt or marks. Dirty means covered in dust, mud or stains.
quests.funFact: Soap helps water lift greasy dirt off your skin so it can be rinsed away.

quests.instruction: The library is very quiet. A fireworks show is very…
quests.hint: Why do people sometimes cover their ears at a big fireworks show?
quests.explanation: Loud sounds are strong and easy to hear from far away. Quiet places have only soft sounds or none at all.
quests.funFact: Sound needs something like air to travel through, so space is silent.

quests.instruction: Zara drank every drop of her juice. Now the glass is…
quests.hint: Tip the glass upside down. Nothing drips out.
quests.explanation: Full means there’s no room for more inside. Empty means there’s nothing inside at all.
quests.funFact: A glass that’s half full holds exactly the same amount as one that’s half empty.

quests.instruction: Ben’s pencil was long on Monday. After a week of sharpening, it is…
quests.hint: What disappears a little each time you use the sharpener?
quests.explanation: Long describes something that stretches far from end to end. After lots of sharpening the pencil’s length has been used up, so it’s short.
quests.funFact: Pencil “lead” is really made of graphite mixed with clay, not the metal lead.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “new”? (a shiny bike fresh from the shop vs. a rusty bike from long ago)
quests.hint: Think of a pair of shoes you’ve worn almost every day for years.
quests.explanation: New means just made or just bought. Old means it has been around, and used, for a long time.
quests.funFact: “News” started out as the plural of “new”, meaning new things.

quests.instruction: Lena’s towel was dry before swimming. When she wrapped it around herself dripping from the pool, it became…
quests.hint: Picture a towel the moment you climb out of the pool.
quests.explanation: Dry means there’s no water on or in something. Wet means it’s soaked with water, like a towel after a swim.
quests.funFact: About 70 percent of Earth’s surface is covered in water.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “soft”? (a fluffy pillow vs. a brick wall)
quests.hint: Would you rather rest your head on a cushion or on a rock?
quests.explanation: Soft things squish or give way when you press them. Hard things stay firm and don’t change shape.
quests.funFact: Diamond is the hardest natural material on Earth.

quests.instruction: A feather is light. A big boulder is…
quests.hint: Which one could the wind carry across the playground?
quests.explanation: Here “light” means easy to lift. The opposite is heavy: a thing that’s hard to carry because it weighs a lot.
quests.funFact: On the Moon, astronauts dropped a hammer and a feather and they hit the ground together.

quests.instruction: The lamp was on while Dad read. Then he flipped the switch and it was…
quests.hint: Imagine a bedroom after goodnight kisses and a click on the wall.
quests.explanation: On means working or switched to run. Off means the power has been turned away from it.
quests.funFact: LED bulbs use far less electricity than old-fashioned bulbs.

quests.instruction: Omar is first in line. Kai is last, so he stands at the…
quests.hint: Where does the end of a queue wait?
quests.explanation: Front is where something begins or faces forward. The back is the part behind everything else.
quests.funFact: The front of a ship is called the bow and the back is called the stern.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “top”? (the highest shelf vs. the lowest shelf)
quests.hint: If you pour out a bag of marbles, where do the last ones roll to?
quests.explanation: The top is the highest part of something. The bottom is the lowest part, the one closest to the ground.
quests.funFact: Mount Everest’s summit is the highest point on Earth above sea level.

quests.instruction: Priya writes with her right hand. Her friend writes with the other one, her…
quests.hint: Hold out both hands: which one makes an “L” with your thumb and finger?
quests.explanation: Left and right are the two sides of your body. If one is the right hand, the other must be the left.
quests.funFact: Roughly one in ten people is left-handed.

quests.instruction: At the zebra crossing, a red light means stop. A green light means…
quests.hint: What do cars do when the light turns the color of grass?
quests.explanation: Stop means don’t move. Go means you may move ahead.
quests.funFact: Red is used for stop signs partly because it’s easy to see from far away.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “awake”? (a child with wide-open eyes vs. a child snoring softly)
quests.hint: Who wouldn’t notice if you turned on the TV next to them?
quests.explanation: Awake means your eyes and mind are switched on. Asleep means your body is resting and you’re not aware of what’s around you.
quests.funFact: Dolphins can sleep with one half of the brain at a time.

quests.instruction: Fresh strawberries taste good. Strawberries left in a hot car for a week taste…
quests.hint: Fruit that has gone mushy and moldy goes straight in the bin.
quests.explanation: Good means nice or as it should be. Bad means not nice, like fruit that has gone off.
quests.funFact: Strawberries are the only fruit with their seeds on the outside.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “near”? (a school across the street vs. a school in another town)
quests.hint: Which trip needs a bus instead of a short walk?
quests.explanation: Near means a short distance away. Far means a long way off.
quests.funFact: The Moon is about 384,000 kilometres from Earth.

quests.instruction: The sky was full of stars last night, but tonight clouds hide most of them. Tonight there are only…
quests.hint: Count the stars you can spot when only a handful peek out.
quests.explanation: Many means a large number. Few means just a small number of things.
quests.funFact: On a dark, clear night you can see about two or three thousand stars with your eyes alone.

quests.instruction: Mia hung her coat on a high hook. Her little brother can only reach a…
quests.hint: Look at the hooks near the door that small arms can actually reach.
quests.explanation: High means far above the ground. Low means close to the ground, where short arms can reach.
quests.funFact: Mount Everest is the highest mountain, while the shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest dry land on Earth.

quests.instruction: A winter coat is thick. A summer T-shirt is…
quests.hint: Why do we wear woolly sweaters in January but not in July?
quests.explanation: Thick means a lot of material from one side to the other. Thin means very little, like the cloth of a summer shirt.
quests.funFact: Wool keeps you warm because it traps tiny pockets of air.

quests.instruction: A ripe mango tastes sweet. A lemon tastes…
quests.hint: Imagine biting a lemon wedge and scrunching up your face.
quests.explanation: Sweet is the sugary taste of things like mango and honey. Sour is the sharp, mouth-puckering taste of lemons.
quests.funFact: Your tongue can taste sweet, sour, salty, bitter and savory.

quests.instruction: The picnic was planned for a sunny day, but a thick grey blanket covered the sky. It turned out…
quests.hint: Something grey and fluffy is blocking the sun. Imagine looking up and seeing only that.
quests.explanation: Sunny means bright sunshine. Cloudy means clouds are covering the sky and blocking the sun.
quests.funFact: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water or ice crystals.

quests.instruction: Two matching socks are the same. A red sock and a blue sock are…
quests.hint: Do these two socks go together as a pair?
quests.explanation: Same means exactly alike. Different means not alike in some way, like colors that don’t match.
quests.funFact: “Different” comes from a Latin word meaning “to set apart”.
